summary.headline: Kalpataru Q1 FY27 pre-sales rose 6% YoY to Rs 1,329 crore, while Q1 revenue of Rs 472 crore produced a Rs 29 crore loss.
summary.overview: Pre-sales grew 6% YoY to Rs 1,329 crore and collections rose 17% YoY to Rs 1,365 crore, with most collections coming from previously sold units. Revenue from operations was Rs 472 crore with adjusted EBITDA of Rs 95 crore (~20% margin) and a net loss of Rs 29 crore, reflecting the project completion method of revenue recognition. Net debt stood at Rs 8,229 crore (net debt/equity ~2.0x) after a Rs 1,800 crore refinancing that cut the weighted average cost of borrowing to ~11%. Management guided FY27 pre-sales of ~Rs 6,500 crore (~23% growth) and expects profit recognition mainly in H2 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +6% YoY (vs Rs 1,249 crore in Q1 FY26)
down ~200 bps since listing; ~Rs 180 crore annual savings cumulative

segments.name: Kalpataru Park City, Thane
segments.commentary: Pre-sales surged ~350% YoY on a low base; more than 2,000 families now reside on-site, with over 3,000 expected by end of next year.

segments.name: Mumbai luxury launch (Kalpataru Vian, Hrushikesh, Lokhandwala)
segments.commentary: Launched late June 2026 with 3, 4 and 4.5 BHK homes on a four-acre enclave in Andheri West; management called the response encouraging, no units quantified.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales target of ~Rs 6,500 crore, ~23% growth over FY26.
Net debt expected to stay around FY26 levels by end FY27; net debt/equity to improve from ~2.0x as profits are recognised at year-end FY27.
Debt trend guided to decline YoY, though quarterly increases possible due to project and BD spend.
Target of 5.5 million sq ft completion in FY27; ~15 million sq ft of ongoing projects to be completed across FY27-FY29.
Launch pipeline of ~5 million sq ft worth ~Rs 7,800 crore this year; new launches expected to contribute ~25% of FY27 sales.
Price increases to be quantified by Q2 as projects progress.
capex_capacity: Two launches in Q1 totalling ~1.25 million sq ft saleable: Tower C of Estella (Kalpataru Park City, Thane) and Kalpataru Vian, Hrushikesh (Lokhandwala, Mumbai).
Occupation certificate received for ~0.79 million sq ft across 668 units in Q1, including Kalpataru Elitus Tower B and Kalpataru Summit Office Complex in Mulund.
Launch timing: Blossom next quarter; Estella 1 Tower this quarter; Hari Niketan this quarter; Ardene and Suman Nagar next quarter.
Secured development agreement for redevelopment of five societies in Ashok Nagar, Kandivali: ~2.8-acre land, GDV potential Rs 1,250 crore.
Monetised commercial office Kalpataru Infinia (Shivajinagar, Pune) for ~Rs 119 crore.
demand_pricing: Area sold rose ~48% YoY but pre-sales grew only 6%; management attributed the lower average realisation to project mix, not discounting.
Booking during the quarter was marginal; most collections came from previously sold units.
New launches contributed 35% of Q1 sales per management.
Management sees positive walk-in and conversion trends and stable-to-strong pricing post the Middle East conflict.
Macro commentary: high-earning end-users upgrading to larger premium homes; global decision cycles slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Area sold up 48% but pre-sales up only 6%: was this project mix or discounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was due to project mix.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Rs 1,365 crore collection came from older receivables versus Q1 bookings?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Joglekar said Q1 bookings were marginal and most collections were from units sold earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt rise from March to June and where was cash deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said debt is directionally expected to fall YoY; intra-quarter increases are possible from project spend and new BD acquisitions.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Rs 1,800-2,000 crore FY27 new-launch sales target has been achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Parag Munot said 35% of Q1 sales came from new sales and full-year new-launch contribution remains ~25%.

qa_highlights.question: Launch timeline across the next three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Launches are spread across the three quarters: Blossom next quarter, Estella 1 Tower and Hari Niketan this quarter, Ardene and Suman Nagar next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Pricing trend post-war and expected price increases for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing described as stable and strong; price increases will be planned as projects progress, with quantification by Q2.

risks_watch: Revenue recognition is back-ended under the project completion method; H2 FY27 profit recognition is critical to the year-end net debt/equity improvement.
Net debt of Rs 8,229 crore and gross debt of Rs 9,189 crore; management guides flat net debt for FY27 despite BD and launch capex.
Realisation pressure: area sold up 48% but pre-sales only up 6%, indicating lower average price per sq ft from mix.
Execution risk on 5.5 million sq ft completion target and launch timelines (Blossom, Ardene, Suman Nagar).
Macro sensitivity from Middle East geopolitical tensions, energy prices and rate trajectory.
Q1 bookings were marginal; sustaining pre-sales requires launches to convert, with ~25% of FY27 sales expected from new launches.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and collections, and on the Thane and Mumbai launches, but vague on specifics such as pricing magnitude and reasons for the rise in debt. Management deferred price-increase quantification to Q2 and gave only directional debt guidance.
key_quotes: We are seeing a positive trend towards walk-ins and conversion and also the pricing is looking stable and strong.
Directionally, it is going to be on the downside, year on year.
The booking made during the quarter was marginal only. Most of the collection was due to the units sold earlier.
